def_enPassant: A special pawn capture: if an enemy pawn moves two squares and lands beside yours, you may capture it as though it had only moved one — but only on your very next move.
def_castlingKingside: A king-and-rook move toward the h-file, getting the king to safety and the rook into play in one move.
def_castlingQueenside: A king-and-rook move toward the a-file — same idea as kingside castling, the other direction.
def_check: Your king is under direct attack. You must get out of check immediately — move the king, block the attack, or capture the attacker.
def_checkmate: A check with no way out. The game ends immediately.
def_stalemate: The player to move has no legal move and is not in check. The game is a draw.
def_fork: One piece attacking two (or more) enemy pieces at the same time, so the opponent can't save them all.
def_pin: A piece can't move (or shouldn't) because doing so would expose a more valuable piece behind it to attack.
def_skewer: Like a pin in reverse: attacking a valuable piece that, if it moves, exposes a less valuable one behind it.
def_discoveredAttack: Moving one piece out of the way reveals an attack from another piece behind it.
def_doubleAttack: A single move that creates two threats at once, so the opponent can only defend against one.
def_zugzwang: A position where any legal move makes things worse for the player to move — they'd rather pass, but chess doesn't allow that.
def_zwischenzug: An 'in-between move' — instead of the expected reply, a player inserts a surprising, more urgent move first.
def_fianchetto: Developing a bishop to the long diagonal by moving it to the square next to a knight, after the knight's pawn has advanced.
def_outpost: A square, usually in enemy territory, where a piece (often a knight) can sit safely because no enemy pawn can ever attack it.
def_isolatedPawn: A pawn with no friendly pawns on either neighboring file to defend it if attacked.
def_passedPawn: A pawn with no enemy pawns in front of it (on its file or the two adjacent files) to stop it from promoting.
def_doubledPawns: Two of your own pawns stacked on the same file — usually a structural weakness.
def_backRankMate: Checkmate delivered along a player's own first rank, because their king had no escape square — typically trapped behind its own pawns.
def_perpetualCheck: A repeating sequence of checks neither side can escape, leading to a draw by repetition.
def_opposition: An endgame king standoff: two kings face off with one square between them, and it's important whose turn it is to move.
def_tempo: A 'move' of relative time — gaining a tempo means getting ahead in development or position for free, often by making a threat the opponent must answer.
def_development: Bringing your pieces out from their starting squares into the game, especially in the opening.
def_material: The total value of the pieces and pawns a player has on the board.
def_centipawn: The engine's unit for measuring advantage — 100 centipawns is roughly worth one pawn.
def_overloadedPiece: A piece defending two things at once, so it can be distracted or removed to win one of them.
def_smotheredMate: Checkmate by a knight against a king that has no escape square because it's completely surrounded by its own pieces.
def_enPrise: A piece that can be captured for free (or for less than it's worth) right now.
def_tactic: A short forcing sequence — checks, captures, threats — that wins material or delivers checkmate.
def_sacrifice: Giving up material on purpose, betting that what you get in return (an attack, a better position, forced mate) is worth more.
